title: revert: "SocketCAN: Treat non-CAN-XL packets with length > 16 bytes as CAN-FD" and drop unusable CAN frame content
description:
This reverts commit d48366c9f9e2f395aa9d3768184f9bcd8cef8b77

In the reverted commit the length of the CAN frame data is used to
distinguish CAN CC frames from CAN FD frames to apparently 'fix' a
defective generated capture file.
There is no way to separate CAN CC/FD frames through their length
information and therefore this patch added a wrong heuristic instead
of dropping and/or notifying the broken capture file content.

See discussion about the merge request:
https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18710

CC: Giovanni Musto <giovanni.musto@partner.italdesign.it>
CC: John Thacker <johnthacker@gmail.com>
CC: Guy Harris <gharris@sonic.net>
Signed-off-by: Oliver Hartkopp <socketcan@hartkopp.net>

notes.body: mentioned in merge request !18710

First of all, thanks for the MR.

By expert info I meant using `proto_tree_add_expert()`.

My idea (let's see if others agree) is to keep the detection as is (i.e. detect unpadded frames without FDF and payload > 8 as CAN-FD), then add an expert info to tell the user this is just our guess, and that their capture is broken.

No. No wrong heuristic. No more words on this really bad idea.

I've tested the code from this MR and it shows the correct CAN CC/FD/XL frames.
![CorrectFD](/uploads/b6cec7012ba9819dc67a3a8e51080f84/CorrectFD.png)


When I load your broken CAN FD capture file it now looks like this: 
![BrokenFD](/uploads/6f9df1a1eccddab1a2b4a99710343c90/BrokenFD.png)

It shows that 40 bytes have been read - but it has correctly not labeled the captured data as any CAN frame.

The question is whether we put some hint into the "Info" section, e.g.
"Unrecognized content (broken capture file?)"

Or do you think this is not even needed?

Because the data to analyze the problem is already visible in the down right window.
I've been reading the somewhat heated argument about this issue and decided to pass for the time being.

Yes. And after all my explanations I'm really fed up that such technically wrong things get merged without having at least asked people like @LarsVoelker and me that have been working on CAN software for years. I have an interest to enable the best CAN support in Wireshark but it is not funny and not my wish to have to fight people that break things because they don't have the entire picture. And after this really lengthy discussion with @giovanni.musto I get heated when he again comes up with "My idea (let's see if others agree) is to keep the detection" which is just wrong and it remains wrong.

The point is that https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18710 introduced a wrong heuristic which should be fixed ASAP before is goes into some (stable) release.

So I have no preference whether @johnthacker, @guyharris or you want to fix it up. Please coordinate with each other. Thanks!

Hi guys, would it be possible to have a few example traces?

I am not really that involved into CAN-XL but from my experience the LINKTYPE_CAN_SOCKETCAN had some weaknesses in the past before that really made it hard to write good Wireshark code. With traces it would be easier to form an opinion.

These are the Wireshark 3.6 capture files from Kernel 5.15
https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18710#note_2300751211
and 6.13-rc
https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18710#note_2300691559 I recorded on my system. They have the PDU size distinction 16 bytes (CC) and 72 bytes (FD).

And here https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/issues/20328 you can find the (broken) capture file from @giovanni.musto which was the reason for the https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18710 merge request. It has a CC frame with 32 data bytes -> 40 bytes PDU length (see screenshot above).

In fact in the latest code base there is no interference with the CAN XL support which looks for the CANXL_XLF flag first (as it later does for the CANFD_FDF flag to detect CAN FD).

It is only about the wrongly generated capture files with the "optimized" length without setting CANFD_FDF flag properly.

Ok, after reading the code and https://www.tcpdump.org/linktypes/LINKTYPE_CAN_SOCKETCAN.html I get what Oliver is saying. He tries to get the official specification implemented and 'broken' packets detect as that. And after having experienced such misdetection with CAN, the value is clear to me.

I also understand the position to be a bit more liberal on parsing. If the trace is broken, you do not want to get the hexeditor out to patch the trace.

Why don't we go for a config option, e.g., like 'Activate strict SocketCAN format' or 'Activate SocketCAN parsing heuristic'?

This would allow to activate the loose parsing, when you know that you have broken files but also allow to have somewhat more strict checks, when needed. If loose parsing is turned on, I would propose to have an expert info for all packets for which the dissector has to 'guess' the format should be marked.

What do you think?

Hello Lars! Thanks for stepping into the discussion.
After reading your comment I had a pretty sleepless night thinking about the usability and the transparency for the user - and how @giovanni.musto might use content from his broken pcapng file recorded sometime in 2017.

My concern about https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18710 is, that it silently and in-transparently modifies content with a heuristic that has no valid entropy to work on.

After having CAN CC for some time the integration of CAN FD relied on the PDU structure length of 16/72 bytes. The data length is picked from a data structure element:
![WiresharkCCFD-length](/uploads/53c0ad149740fd86de494d6224a41dde/WiresharkCCFD-length.png)
Then someone "optimized" the length to store the CAN frames which killed the "distinction by PDU structure length" and led to broken PCAPNG files where the information about CAN FD can not be retrieved anymore:
![WiresharkCCFD-broken](/uploads/15183482a09c06158db626f3e47a90db/WiresharkCCFD-broken.png)
Later the code for the "optimized" length handling was fixed by ensuring the FDF flag to mark CAN FD frames and have a proper distinction again:
![WiresharkCCFD-flags](/uploads/2a6e0eee663abe609c0fe2435f76a748/WiresharkCCFD-flags.png)

So how to handle e.g. @giovanni.musto 's PCAPNG files from the broken period?

Before https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18710 the output of the three examples was:

1. FD32 -> CC32
2. FD6 -> CC6
3. CC6 -> CC6

Where the FD32 is visibly wrong and FD6 is invisibly wrong. But this was expected from the missing CAN FD identification.

After https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18710 the output of the three examples is:

1. FD32 -> FD32
2. FD6 -> CC6
3. CC6 -> CC6

Where the FD32 is ok but FD6 becomes visibly wrong. Additionally the user is not informed about the modification.

With my patch set from https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18831 the output of the three examples is:

1. FD32 -> no detected as a CAN frame but visible in the GUI as 40 byte PDU
2. FD6 -> CC6
3. CC6 -> CC6

Only FD6 remains invisibly wrong.

Finally all those solutions are somehow bad as we simply can not "repair" such under-specified PCAPNG files. We can only make it "less bad".

From my perspective we have three options after detecting the obviously wrong CC32 frame in the data stream where we should open some GUI dialog and ask for the user preference for this specific PCAPNG file:

1. Ignore the length check for CC frames (behavior before https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18710)
2. Detect all frames as CAN FD type frames (also real CC frames)
3. Abort the processing of the PCAPNG file

If we do not want to overload Wireshark with the handling of undecodable PCAPNG files, we might also abort the processing of the PCAPNG file and point to some documentation about this issue - and maybe provide a script that modifies the "all frames as CAN FD type frames" flag with the existing pcap editing tools.

In any case the user has to be clear that he has a broken capture file and he has to make a qualified decision to match his requirements best.

btw.

I was wondering where people even get broken traces. I let some of our teams check some of the other tools we wrote and our BLF Converter [1] seems to also not set the Flag for CAN-FD. :disappointed:

We are working on a patch to fix this.

[1] https://github.com/Technica-Engineering/Technica.Traces.Blf.Converter/

> I was wondering where people even get broken traces.

I assume in this case it was created by Wireshark/libpcap right after the "optimized length" has been introduced (without FDF flag support).

> our BLF Converter [1] seems to also not set the Flag for CAN-FD.

Hm, I tried to build https://github.com/Technica-Engineering/Technica.Traces.Blf.Converter/ and https://github.com/Technica-Engineering/vector_blf/ before but I ended with

```
CMake Error at vector_blf/CMakeLists.txt:11 (add_library):
  No SOURCES given to target: Vector_BLF
```
In Technica.Traces.Blf.Converter/build/_deps/pcapng_exporter-src/pcapng_exporter.cpp the struct canfd_frame is used. But I'm not sure how the CAN CC frame is generated then ...

Did you try to read a mix of CAN CC/FD frames generated by your BLF converter into a recent Wireshark?

Before you build, you need to pull in the submodule(s):
```
git submodule init
git submodule update
```

It seems that the BLF Converter does not set the Flag for CAN-FD and does not pad to 72 Bytes. That is a problem. We have created an internal ticket and prepare a patch.

The TECMP Converter looks fine.


So people that are using our BLF Converter would generate such bad traces. We created that long before I added BLF to Wireshark. So I am not even sure, if it is used that often.

All,

what are your suggestions about my summary?
https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18831#note_2322199172
Gentle ping?

If you are unsure what to do, please simply revert the problematic commit
https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/commit/d48366c9f9e2f395aa9d3768184f9bcd8cef8b77

And we can later start to discus how to handle faulty generated capture files better - without pressure.

Thanks!
Sorry, I will take a look, I was seeing if anyone else had an opinion on the subject.
Thanks @johnthacker !

commits_data.message:
socketcan: drop unusable CAN frames

The different CAN CC/FD/XL frames can be decoded by means of length
information and specific bits. Content that does not fit these properties
is not usable.

TODO: Create some expert information to notify such content.

Signed-off-by: Oliver Hartkopp <socketcan@hartkopp.net>
